answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable stake locked for weeks before it can earn, like a saffron harvest that only pays after the season: one fake identity is cheap, but a meadow of thousands each locking real funds becomes ruinously expensive, and the stake is slashed if the identity misbehaves. A reputation inlet that only admits agents with a history of completed, attested work raises the cost further, because an attacker must buy time and honest history for every fake, not just spin up a new keypair.
